newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy pledges continued support to Albania.
newsitem.headline: Italy pledges continued support to Albania.

text.p: Italy urged Albania's new president on Friday to continue rapidly along the path to democracy and pledged continued solidarity with its lawless Balkan neighbour.

"Italy fervently hopes Albania can rapidly conclude its processes of normalisation and consolidation of democratic institutions," Italian President Oscar Luigi Scalfaro said in a letter to his new Albanian counterpart, Rexhep Mejdani.

"Italy will continue to offer its determined support to the Albanian nation, in the spirit of collaboration and solidarity that has always characterised relations between our two nations," he said in his message.
Italy has been leading a 7,000-strong international security force in Albania. The force is expected to complete its withdrawal by August 12. Italian troops started pulling out last week.

Albania's parliament on Thursday elected Mejdani, the Socialist Party secretary-general, as president. He replaces Sali Berisha, who had resigned the previous day after his Democratic Party's electoral defeat by the Socialist Party.
The elections were called to end months of anarchy in Albania triggered by the collapse of pyramid savings schemes in which thousands lost their life savings.
Mejdani has moved fast to install a new administration. He asked Socialist Party chairman Fatos Nano on Thursday to form a government, and Nano presaented his cabinet to the president on Friday.
